world.b: The Houthis are threatening Saudi ports over the coalition's Hodeidah evacuation order. Follow Al Jazeera's live coverage of the US-Israel war on Iran.
world.title: Iran says another tanker on fire after hitting mine in Hormuz

world.b: The International Campaign to Ban Landmines recorded 6,929 casualties in 2025, 84% of them civilians, driven largely by Myanmar's civil war.

world.h: UN: 47,000 women killed by partners or family
world.b: About 47,000 women and girls were killed by an intimate partner or family member last year, the UN's 2026 Femicide Brief found, and home remains the most dangerous place for them.

national.h: FDA to expand testing of prescription drugs
national.b: The FDA will test more drugs for impurities and quality lapses after a ProPublica investigation found it rarely tested generics doctors had flagged.
national.title: FDA to Expand Prescription Drug Testing After ProPublica Revealed Safety Concerns

national.h: Army calls Iowa lead azide detonation a success
national.b: Army officials said Wednesday's controlled detonation of 68 drums of volatile lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant 'wildly exceeded' expectations.
national.title: US Army declares Iowa lead azide detonation ‘tremendously successful’

national.h: Kilmar Abrego Garcia self-deports to Spain
national.b: Abrego Garcia, wrongfully deported to El Salvador last year, left voluntarily after months fighting a second deportation to Africa.

national.h: Alaska ends voter records deal with DOJ
national.b: Lt. Gov. Nancy Dahlstrom withdrew Alaska from a 2025 agreement giving the Justice Department access to state voter rolls.

national.h: Iran suspected in hacks of up to 50 ships
national.b: US officials are investigating cyberattacks that compromised as many as 50 commercial vessels as potentially linked to Iran.

national.h: Paxton drops cases against trans care doctors
national.b: Outgoing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton dropped lawsuits against two doctors accused of violating the state's ban on transgender youth care.

national.h: Princeton researcher held by ICE at D.C. airport
national.b: ICE detained Chinese doctoral student Eva Yi Xie at Reagan National Airport; DHS says she overstayed her visa.

national.h: ProPublica: Ambetter prior authorization hurt patients
national.b: A ProPublica investigation found the popular insurance plan's use of prior authorization led to delayed cancer treatment and missed medication.
national.title: Delayed Cancer Treatment. Missed Medication. How a Popular Insurance Plan’s Use of Prior Authorization Hurt Patients.

national.h: Doctors struggle as parents refuse vitamin K
national.b: At a Grand Rapids hospital, at least one family a day on average refuses the vitamin K injection for their newborn.

national.h: Medical debt could get worse, experts warn
national.b: Millions of Americans carry medical debt, and experts worry high inflation, health costs and lost insurance will push the number higher.
national.title: Millions of Americans have medical debt. Experts worry the problem is about to get worse

national.b: The state health department confirmed the death of an unvaccinated Centre County resident who tested positive for measles, bringing the outbreak's death toll to nine.

national.h: Trump calls to speed up federal executions
national.b: At the Justice Department, Trump reaffirmed his support for the death penalty and attacked California Gov. Gavin Newsom.

politics.h: Poll: Most voters want Iran war ended now
politics.b: A new poll finds a majority of US voters want the war on Iran to end immediately, even on less favorable terms.

politics.h: Blanche won't say if Huang was investigated
politics.b: Attorney General Todd Blanche declined to say whether the Justice Department investigated Nvidia's Jensen Huang.

politics.h: Pentagon weighs $15B loan to Trump Jr.-linked startup
politics.b: ProPublica reports the Pentagon is considering a $15 billion loan to Hadrian Automation, which recently got a major investment from Trump Jr.'s venture firm.
politics.title: A Startup Tied to Donald Trump Jr. Could Get a Historic $15 Billion Loan From the Pentagon

politics.h: Abortion-rights Democrats won, but big changes unlikely
politics.b: Democrats lack full control in states with the strictest bans, and any congressional move would likely face a Trump veto.
Democrats eyeing the White House see Trump's pressure on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as fresh evidence of his coziness with tech executives.

politics.h: Unsealed records detail search of Ilhan Omar's home
politics.b: Court documents show the magistrate judge who approved the search ruled Omar could assert privacy protections for sitting members of Congress.

politics.h: Democrats widen probe of Trump Jr.-linked firm
politics.b: Led by Rep. Jamie Raskin, Democrats are expanding their investigation into 1789 Capital, which investigators say grew from $150 million to $3 billion in managed assets after Trump Jr. joined.
As counting wraps up in the final midterm races, Democrats hold 258 of 435 House seats with four races uncalled, and the party plans to use its majorities for oversight.

international.h: Tinubu vows peace for Nigeria's northeast ahead of vote
international.b: At a rally in Maiduguri, President Bola Tinubu promised to restore peace to the rebellion-hit region as he seeks a second term on January 16.
international.title: Nigeria’s Tinubu pledges to bring peace to rebellion-hit border region

international.h: Ecuador and US review joint military operations
international.b: The US paused operations in Ecuador pending an investigation into one carried out by Ecuadoran forces that raised human rights questions.
international.title: Ecuador and US review joint military operations, official says

international.h: UK moves warplanes into hangars over drone threat
international.b: British outlets report the RAF is sheltering planes overnight and installing anti-drone nets; the Ministry of Defence says it takes base security very seriously.
international.title: UK military ‘moving aircraft to hangars in case of drone attacks’

international.h: Fuel truck fire kills at least 30 on Cairo ring road
international.b: A vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire above a tunnel in Giza's Warraq district, Egypt's health ministry said; 15 were injured.
international.title: At least 30 killed in Egypt vehicle fire, health ministry says

international.h: Iraq's top court lets Baghdad take over Kurdish borders
international.b: The ruling lets federal troops deploy to borders in the Kurdish region, a day after the prime minister ordered forces to take over Kurdish-run crossings and oil fields.
international.title: Iraq’s top court rules government can take over Kurdish borders, oil fields

international.h: Solomon Islands bars foreign bases in Australia treaty
international.b: Solomon Islands signed a sweeping treaty with Australia affirming it will allow no foreign military bases, seen as a blow to China's regional ambitions.

international.h: Puigdemont to return to Spain on December 12
international.b: The Catalan separatist leader says he will end nearly a decade of exile after Spain's Supreme Court applied the amnesty law and shelved his case.

international.h: RSF drone attacks kill at least 19 in Sudan's Blue Nile
international.b: A rights group said Rapid Support Forces drones struck Damazin late Tuesday, killing at least 19 people and wounding at least 20.

international.h: Israeli strike kills Gaza security official and family
international.b: Gaza's Interior Ministry said an Israeli air attack killed Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, head of internal security in northern Gaza, with his wife and two daughters.

international.h: Two Libyan officers die after drone strike on Russian ship
international.b: Eastern Libyan forces said two naval officers died of wounds from Ukraine's drone attack on a Russian warship near Benghazi.

international.h: Saudi Arabia downs Houthi drones
international.b: Saudi air defenses destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura, a day after a coalition air strike on Hodeidah; no casualties were initially reported.

international.h: Dozens feared trapped in flooded Indonesia mine
international.b: Rescuers are searching for workers trapped after an overflowing river flooded an unauthorized open-pit gold mine in West Java's Bogor district.

international.h: UK warns firms of Russian sabotage threat
international.b: The Defence Ministry and security officials warned companies supplying Ukraine's military that they could be targets of Russian sabotage.

international.h: Bangladesh garment workers win 36% raise
international.b: After months of protests, the wage board agreed to lift the sector's minimum wage from 12,500 to 17,500 taka a month.

international.h: Eisenkot lands first coalition partner
international.b: Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party agreed to a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman's party in a bid to form Israel's next government.

international.h: WHO chief urges end to US fuel blockade on Cuba
international.b: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned the sanctions endanger children's lives as fuel shortages strain Cuba's healthcare system.

international.h: Pentagon rebukes Canada over military spending
international.b: A blunt Defense Department fact sheet said Canada falls short as a partner in defending North America; Ottawa says it has committed C$81.8 billion to rebuild its forces.

international.h: Rebels pull back in eastern DR Congo
international.b: The CRP rebel group led by Thomas Lubanga said it halted its advance toward Bunia, Ituri's capital, after days of heavy fighting with government forces.

international.h: South Africa convicts man who tried to fight for Russia
international.b: Zimbabwean Tafadzwa Sithole received a suspended five-year sentence for trying to travel to Russia to fight in Ukraine and will be deported.

international.h: Colombia blames ex-FARC rebels for car bomb
international.b: President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed FARC dissident commander Antonio Medina for a car bomb at a state government building in Villavicencio that injured at least 23.

international.h: Cameroon separatist pleads not guilty in Norway
international.b: Lucas Cho Ayaba denied charges in an Oslo court of being an accessory to war crimes and terrorism over two attacks in Cameroon.

international.h: Putin vows retaliation over refinery strikes
international.b: Putin said Ukraine kept attacking Russian oil refineries despite Trump's requests to hold off, and threatened retaliation.

international.h: Turkish military helicopter crash kills five
international.b: An air force AS-532 helicopter crashed after taking off from Eskisehir on a training flight, killing five crew members, the defense ministry said.

international.h: Pope Francis' diary reveals spiritual crisis
international.b: Diary excerpts published by the Vatican describe Francis seeing the 'gates of hell' over the abuse scandal and a spiritual crisis in 2021-22.

international.h: UK heat deaths hit record high
international.b: The UK Health Security Agency estimates more than 5,000 deaths were linked to this summer's heat, the most since its reports began in 2016.

international.h: Projectile hits Riyadh tower, injuring 11
international.b: Saudi Civil Defence said an unspecified projectile struck a tower in Riyadh's financial district, injuring 11 people.

international.h: Two arrested after break-in at Prince William's home
international.b: Police arrested two men on suspicion of burglary and trespass after a break-in at Anmer Hall on the Sandringham estate; the house was unoccupied.

international.h: China probes Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
international.b: The Politburo member is the fourth from the top leadership body investigated since last year, suspected of 'severe violations of discipline and laws,' Xinhua said.

international.h: Malaysia to send 6,500 Rohingya back to Myanmar
international.b: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced the repatriations five days after the World Court ruled Myanmar's forces committed genocide against the Rohingya.

international.h: Hasina plans Dec. 16 return to Bangladesh
international.b: Ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, sentenced to death in absentia, plans to return from exile in India; the government says she can only return through extradition.

international.h: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill at least 7
international.b: At least seven Palestinians, including a child and police officers, were killed in Israeli air strikes on Gaza as doctors warn of a meningitis outbreak.

international.h: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills two
international.b: A dawn air attack killed two people and wounded more than 40, including an infant, a day after Kyiv said its drones sank a Russian warship in a Libyan port.

international.h: Australia threatens tech giants with big fines
international.b: Communications Minister Anika Wells announced plans for heavier fines on tech companies that fail to remove harmful content from their platforms.

international.h: Guterres urges global AI oversight within a year
international.b: Speaking at a conference in Barbados, the UN secretary-general called on member states to build a multilateral AI risk framework backed by independent oversight within the next year.

international.h: Bukele names soldiers killed in Haiti
international.b: El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele identified the three Salvadoran soldiers killed on an anti-gang mission in Haiti.

international.h: Mexico to try 'El Chapo Isidro' at home
international.b: Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said alleged cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores will be tried in Mexico despite a US extradition request.

business.h: Portland man's free newsletter tracks grocery prices
business.b: Bryan Vance has tracked 20 staples at more than a dozen stores since April 2025 in his Stumptown Savings newsletter, as food costs climb.
business.title: Amid rising food costs, a free newsletter is helping a community find deals

business.h: Trump administration plans new tariffs on China, EU and others
business.b: The proposal adds 20% to tariffs on Chinese goods and raises them on the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and nine other trading partners.
business.title: Trump administration to raise tariffs on China, EU, Brazil and others

business.h: Key inflation gauge rises to 3.8% in October
business.b: The Commerce Department said consumer prices rose 3.8% from a year earlier, up from 3.6% in September, even as gas price increases slowed.
business.title: Inflation remains stubbornly high, despite a drop in gas prices

business.h: Dollar Tree bets on wider range of products
business.b: After strong quarterly earnings, the discount retailer says adding items above a dollar lets it offer more brands, price points and pack sizes.

business.h: AI shopping agents can make costly mistakes
business.b: The NRF says 59% of shoppers plan to use AI this holiday weekend, but AI agents can hallucinate and work best when handed more personal data.
business.title: What to know before using AI agents for Black Friday shopping

business.h: Thieves turn to cyber tricks for cargo theft
business.b: Planet Money looks at how sophisticated criminals are stealing truckloads of food and goods, from bourbon to turkey, and why the FBI struggles to catch them.
business.title: How to steal a truckload of bourbon and not get caught : Planet Money

business.b: Steep discounts and oversupply are pushing cannabis prices down ahead of one of the industry's biggest sales days, squeezing retailers.
business.title: In a time of rising costs, one Thanksgiving commodity is cheaper: cannabis

business.h: Asian markets dive on AI doubts
business.b: Asian stocks fell sharply, reversing a rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO.

business.h: Data centers help prop up US manufacturing
business.b: Despite high energy costs and tariffs, manufacturing is holding steady or growing in several Fed districts, helped by data center construction.

business.h: Best Buy posts best growth in five years
business.b: Best Buy grew more than 6% in the third quarter, nearly triple estimates, as pandemic-era laptops and TVs wear out.

business.h: Jury finds Huawei guilty of trade secret conspiracy
business.b: A US jury convicted Huawei of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud.

business.h: Afghan refugees build businesses in Houston
business.b: Thousands of Afghans who resettled in the Houston area after the 2021 US withdrawal have built a growing network of businesses.

business.h: Nvidia recovers most of its lost value
business.b: Nvidia had regained $952 billion of the $1.16 trillion in market value it lost when Jensen Huang resigned, according to a Financial Times analysis.

business.h: Few US homes are protected against floods
business.b: Very few homeowners outside flood zones buy flood insurance, even as storms bring flooding to the Bay Area, the East Coast and Florida.

business.h: Inside Trump's latest meme coin dinner
business.b: Two crypto investors who attended the president's meme coin dinner on Sunday gave NPR inside access; the dinners have sparked intense controversy.

science.h: Rare nearby supernova draws telescopes worldwide
science.b: Astronomers caught type Ia supernova SN 2026ahvu before it peaked, giving an early look at how these stellar explosions work.
science.title: A cosmically close supernova may spill the stellar explosion’s secrets

science.h: Australia's legless geckos evolved like snakes
science.b: Researchers found the 50 species of pygopod geckos, from Australia and New Guinea, show diet and body diversity patterns that resemble snakes'.
science.title: Australia's legless geckos evolved like snakes did

science.h: FCC approves SpaceX plan for 1 million orbiting data centers
science.b: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy 1,000,000 orbital compute modules, called Starmind, to meet growing demand for AI computing.
science.title: US grants SpaceX approval for 1 million space data centres

science.h: Ancient grasshoppers may have walked on water
science.b: Leg hairs preserved in 99-million-year-old amber suggest a newfound family of grasshoppers could skate on surface tension like water striders.
science.title: Extinct, long-legged grasshoppers walked on water alongside dinosaurs

science.h: NOAA: Just one Atlantic hurricane this year
science.b: The 2026 season had 10 named storms and only one hurricane, the fewest hurricanes in the satellite era; forecasters say a repeat is unlikely.

science.h: Eagles may have hunted adult baboons
science.b: Raptor damage on adult male baboon bones from Chad suggests birds of prey can take primates as big as some early human ancestors.
science.title: Eagles can prey on adult baboons. Did our ancestors face that threat?

science.h: After surgery, man sees his cat's eyes on people
science.b: Following 2024 brain surgery, a 29-year-old teacher began seeing features of faces he'd seen before, including his cat's eyes, on other people's faces.
science.title: This man sometimes sees his cat’s eyes on people’s faces

sports.h: Senegal gets Africa Cup title back
sports.b: The Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned a ruling that had handed the Africa Cup of Nations trophy to Morocco after Senegal's players walked off.

goodnews.b: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali docked at China's Tiangong space station, becoming the first foreign astronaut to board it, as Pakistan celebrated.

local.h: Activists sue to stop Greenpoint waterfront towers
local.b: Friends of Bushwick Inlet Park say the 1,300-unit Monitor Point project sits in a floodplain and relies on outdated climate projections.
local.title: Brooklyn environmentalists sue to block Greenpoint waterfront development

local.h: Driver charged in killing of Brooklyn nurse
local.b: Police say Justin Mercado ran a red light at 55 mph on Third Avenue in August, killing 28-year-old nurse Jiayi Zheng in a crosswalk.
local.title: Driver charged with killing Brooklyn nurse crossing Third Avenue

local.h: High wind warning issued for Thanksgiving parade
local.b: Winds will build overnight and peak Thursday afternoon, with up to 2 inches of rain and coastal flooding, putting the parade's balloons at risk.
local.title: Thanksgiving Day forecast upgraded to a high wind warning ahead of parade

local.b: A Manhattan judge rejected landlords' bid to block the two-year rent freeze for about 1 million stabilized apartments, a win for Mayor Mamdani.
local.title: Judge upholds NYC rent freeze, marking win for Mamdani and his affordability agenda

local.h: NYPD seeks six after group exits Manhattan manhole
local.b: Police say five people climbed out of a sewer at 2nd Avenue and East 17th Street on Nov. 18 and left in a red sedan driven by a sixth.
local.title: NYPD searches for 6 sewer spelunkers seen exiting a Manhattan manhole

local.h: Queens DA Katz sues to block wrongful-conviction probe
local.b: Katz argues the state's new prosecutorial conduct commission is unconstitutional as it seeks records on three men wrongly convicted under former DA Richard Brown.
local.title: Queens DA Katz seeks to block prosecutor watchdog investigating wrongful convictions

local.h: Boy, 4, dies in New Jersey house fire
local.b: A 4-year-old boy died and two people were injured in a house fire Tuesday in Union Township, near Newark.
local.title: 4-year-old boy dies, 2 others injured in NJ house fire

local.h: Council summons colleges on sexual assault
local.b: The City Council wants presidents of the 10 largest colleges to testify under oath Dec. 8 about handling campus sexual assaults.
local.title: NYC Council looks for colleges to testify about sexual assault procedures

local.h: Panel to vote on $8B Queens casino design
local.b: The Public Design Commission will vote Monday on the Hard Rock casino complex next to Citi Field after postponing in October.
local.title: NYC panel set to vote on $8 billion Queens casino design Monday

local.h: Body shop owner charged in tow truck scheme
local.b: Brooklyn prosecutors say Steven Ventura used unlicensed tow trucks to haul crash victims' cars and demand bogus storage fees.
local.title: Brooklyn body shop owner charged with bilking drivers in illegal tow truck scheme

local.h: Woman stabbed at random in Riverside Park
local.b: Police are searching for a man who stabbed a 26-year-old woman near West 96th Street Monday night; she is in stable condition.
local.title: NYPD searches for suspect who police say stabbed a woman at random in Riverside Park

local.h: Lawsuit says co-signer firm inflates rents
local.b: A class action accuses TheGuarantors of raising renters' costs through exclusive deals with landlords that block cheaper options.
local.title: NYC renters face ‘higher fees, reduced housing access’ due to co-signer company, lawsuit says

local.h: Report backs regular taxi fare hikes
local.b: A Taxi and Limousine Commission report says yellow cab operating costs rose about 16% since 2022, and regular fare hikes could help drivers avoid poverty.
local.title: Fare hikes on yellow taxi cabs could keep drivers out of poverty, city report finds

periods.name: Tonight
periods.text: Cloudy, with a low around 47. Breezy, with a northeast wind 14 to 24 mph.

periods.name: Thanksgiving Day
periods.text: Rain. The rain could be heavy at times.  High near 60. Windy, with a northeast wind 28 to 34 mph, with gusts as high as 55 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 100%. New precipitation amounts between 1 and 2 inches possible.

periods.name: Thursday Night
periods.text: Rain, mainly before 1am.  Temperature rising to around 60 by 3am. Windy, with an east wind 29 to 34 mph becoming southeast 17 to 22 mph after midnight. Winds could gust as high as 49 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 100%. New precipitation amounts between three quarters and one inch possible.

periods.name: Friday
periods.text: A 50 percent chance of showers.  Mostly cloudy, with a temperature falling to around 54 by 4pm. Breezy, with a south wind 17 to 20 mph.

periods.name: Friday Night
periods.text: Mostly cloudy, with a steady temperature around 52. West wind around 18 mph.

periods.name: Saturday
periods.text: Mostly sunny, with a high near 55.

localgood.h: Van Wyck expansion wraps before Thanksgiving
localgood.b: The state finished the six-year, $1.4 billion project adding lanes and ramps and fixing 23 bridges on the road to JFK.
localgood.title: Queens drivers give thanks as Van Wyck work wraps ahead of busy season at JFK Airport

localgood.b: Green-Wood Cemetery fellows are sifting soil to catalogue potentially thousands of unknown fungus species.
localgood.title: Digging up a secret world under a Brooklyn graveyard, one teaspoon at a time
